title: Field-coordinate hyperplanes, divisors and reduced point
statement: For every field $K$ and $n\geq0$, polynomial projective space $\mathbf P^n_K$ has coordinate geometry [def-pur-projective-bundle-tautological-data]: if $n\geq1$, the zero subscheme of $T_0$ is relative $\mathbf P^{n-1}_K$ over $K$; its complementary standard open is $\mathbf A^n_K$ with ratios $T_{i+1}/T_0$. Every coordinate zero divisor is effective Cartier with dual ideal isomorphic to $\mathcal O(1)$. The scheme-theoretic intersection $T_1=\cdots=T_n=0$ is isomorphic over $K$ to $\operatorname{Spec}K$, is reduced and lies in the zeroth chart. For $n=0$ the intersection is the whole one-coordinate projective space and no hyperplane assertion is required.

proof.text: Obtain the hyperplane identification from [lem-pur-projective-bundle-coordinate-subschemes]. Use the proved CoordinateSectionChart and ChartPolynomial APIs directly; the asserted standard-charts packaging theorem is unnecessary. Obtain the affine chart by reindexing ProjectiveSpace.standardOpenIso with the successor-coordinate equivalence; the functorial appLE identities prove the coordinate ratios. On each standard chart the coordinate ideal is generated by T_i/T_j, which is 1 or a polynomial variable; map regularity through chartRingEquiv. Hom.nonempty_iso_dual_toModules_tensorObj identifies the dual divisor ideal with O(1). The coordinate intersection lies in the zeroth chart because every other chart makes one of its defining equations invertible. On the zeroth chart, the intersection ideal is the image under chartRingEquiv of the ideal generated by all polynomial variables. Evaluation at zero descends to the quotient, and constants are its inverse, by MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext. Ideal.quotientEquiv transfers the bijective constants map to the chart section quotient. The unique surviving subscheme-cover chart is an isomorphism by its full opensRange. The subscheme-cover structural-map equation identifies the structure morphism with Spec of the bijective constants map, hence proves it an isomorphism. This implies reducedness. These fields assemble the required record.
